1
李清臣
Li Qingchen
2
李清臣，字邦直，魏人也。 七歲知讀書，日數千言，暫經目輒誦，稍能戲為文章。 客有從京師來者，與其兄談佛寺火，清臣從傍應曰：「此所謂災也，或者其蠹民已甚，天固儆之邪？ 」因作《浮圖災解》。 兄驚曰：「是必大吾門。 」韓琦聞其名，以兄之子妻之。
Li Qingchen, courtesy name Bangzhi, was a native of Wei. At seven he could read; each day he worked through thousands of characters, and whatever he briefly glanced at he could recite from memory; he could also compose essays with some ease. A visitor from the capital was discussing a temple fire with his elder brother when Qingchen chimed in from the side: "This is what people call a disaster—perhaps the monks have preyed on the people too long, and Heaven is sending a warning?" He then wrote an essay entitled "On the Calamity of Buddhist Pagodas." His brother exclaimed in amazement, "This boy will surely bring great honor to our family." When Han Qi heard of him, he gave Qingchen his nephew's daughter in marriage.
3
舉進士，調邢州司戶參軍、和川令。 歲滿，薦者逾十數，應得京官。 適舉將薛向有公事未竟，閡銓格，判銓張掞擿使自陳勿用。 清臣曰：「人以家保己而己舍之，薄矣。 願待之。 」掞離席曰：「君能如是，未可量也。 」應材識兼茂科，歐陽修壯其文，以比蘇軾。 治平二年，試秘閣，考官韓維曰：「荀卿氏筆力也。 」試文至中書，修迎語曰：「不置李清臣於第一，則謬矣。 」啟視如言。
After passing the jinshi examination, he was posted as revenue clerk at Xingzhou and magistrate of Hechuan. When his term ended, more than ten sponsors recommended him, and he was eligible for promotion to a capital post. At that time Xue Xiang, who was to present the nomination, still had unfinished official business, which blocked the personnel rules; Zhang Shan, chief examiner of the board, seized on the point and had Qingchen declare that he should not be appointed. Qingchen said, "When others rely on family ties to protect themselves, it would be petty of me to abandon them." I would rather wait for him. Zhang Shan rose from his seat and said, "A man who can act as you do cannot yet be measured." He entered the Exceptional Talent and Outstanding Ability examination; Ouyang Xiu admired his prose and compared him to Su Shi. In 1065 he sat for the Secret Pavilion examination. Examiner Han Wei remarked, "This is the pen of Xunzi himself." When the papers reached the Central Secretariat, Ouyang Xiu greeted the examiners and said, "It would be absurd not to place Li Qingchen first." When they opened the papers and reviewed them, it proved exactly as he had predicted.
4
時大雨霖，災異數見，論者歸咎濮議。 及廷對，或謂曰：「宜以《五行傳》『簡宗廟，水不潤下』為證，必擢上第。 」清臣曰：「此漢儒附會之說也，吾不之信。 民間豈無疾痛可上者乎？ 」即條對言：「天地之大，譬如人一身，腹心肺腑有所攻塞，則五官為之不寧。 民人生聚，天地之腹心肺腑也； 日月星辰，天地之五官也。 善止天地之異者，不止其異，止民之疾痛而已。 」策入等，以秘書郎簽書平江軍判官，名聲籍甚。 英宗知之，語王廣淵曰：「韓琦固忠臣，但避嫌太審。 如李清臣者，公議皆謂可用，顧以親抑之可乎？ 」既而詔舉館閣，歐陽修薦之，得集賢校理、同知太常禮院。
At the time torrential rains persisted and portents multiplied; commentators blamed the controversy over Emperor Yingzong's natural father. When the palace examination came, someone advised him: "You should cite the Treatise on the Five Phases—'When ancestral temples are curtailed, water fails to descend'—as proof; that will surely win you the highest honors." Qingchen replied, "That is a forced reading by Han scholastics—I do not accept it. Surely there are grievances among the people worthy of being brought before the throne?" Surely there are grievances among the people worthy of being brought before the throne? He then answered point by point: "Heaven and earth in their immensity are like a single body; when the belly, heart, and lungs are obstructed, the five senses grow restless." The living masses of the people are the belly and heart of heaven and earth; The sun, moon, and stars are heaven and earth's five senses. To truly quell the signs of heaven and earth, one does not suppress the portents themselves but relieves the people's suffering. His examination essay placed among the top ranks, and he was appointed secretary and signing military judge at Pingjiang Circuit; his reputation soared. Emperor Yingzong took note and said to Wang Guangyuan, "Han Qi is a loyal minister, to be sure, but he is excessively cautious about avoiding suspicion. Someone like Li Qingchen is widely regarded as fit for office—can we really hold him back merely because he is a relative?" Before long an edict called for nominations to the Academies; Ouyang Xiu recommended him, and he was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
5
時熙、豐法度，一切厘正，清臣固爭之，罷為資政殿學士、知河陽，徙河南、永興。 召為吏部尚書，給事中姚勔駁之，改知真定府。 班行有王宗正者，致憾於故帥，使其妻詣使者，告前後饋餉過制，囚繫數百人。 清臣至，立奏解其獄，而竄宗正。 帝親政，拜中書侍郎，勔復駁之，不聽。
When the Xining and Yuanfeng reforms were being systematically overhauled, Qingchen objected strenuously and was removed, made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Henan and Yongxing. He was recalled to serve as minister of personnel, but drafting reviewer Yao Miao blocked the appointment; the emperor reassigned him as prefect of Zhending. A clerk named Wang Zongzheng, nursing a grudge against the former prefect, sent his wife to denounce him to the imperial envoy for repeatedly giving gifts beyond what regulations allowed; several hundred people were thrown into prison. When Qingchen took up the post, he immediately petitioned to free them and had Wang Zongzheng exiled. When the emperor began to rule in his own right, Qingchen was appointed vice director of the Secretariat; Yao Miao objected again, but the emperor overruled him.
6
紹聖元年，廷試進士，清臣發策曰：「今復詞賦之選而士不知勸，罷常平之官而農不加富，可差可募之說雜而役法病，或東或北之論異而河患滋，賜土以柔遠也而羌夷之患未弭，弛利以便民也而商賈之路不通。 夫可則因，否則革，惟當之為貴，聖人亦何有必焉。 」主意皆絀元祐之政，策士悟其指，於是紹述之論大興，國是遂變。
In 1094, at the palace examination for new jinshi, Qingchen set the policy question: "Poetry and prose have been restored to the examinations, yet scholars are not motivated to excel; Ever-Normal Granary offices have been abolished, yet farmers are no richer; debate over corvée and hired labor has muddied the labor-service law; conflicting plans for the Yellow River only worsen its floods; land grants meant to pacify frontier peoples have not stilled Qiang and tribal unrest; and easing commercial restrictions to help the people has failed to open trade routes." What works should be kept; what fails should be changed—fitness is all that matters, and even sages impose no fixed dogma. The thrust of the questions was to repudiate Yuanyou policy; candidates grasped the hint, the "continuing the legacy" movement surged, and the direction of the state shifted.
7
范純仁去位，清臣獨顓中書，亟復青苗、免役法，除諸路提舉官。 覬為相，顧蘇轍軋己，乃擿轍嘗以漢武比先帝激上怒，轍罷。 時召章惇未至，清臣心益覬之。 已而惇入相，復與為異。 惇既逐諸臣，並籍文彥博、呂公著以下三十人，將悉竄嶺表。 清臣曰：「更先帝法度，不為無過，然皆累朝元老，若從惇言，必大駭物聽。 」帝曰：「是豈無中道耶？ 合揭榜朝堂，置餘人不問。 」鄜延路金明砦主將張興戰沒，惇怒，議盡戮全軍四千人。 清臣曰：「將死亦多端，或先登爭利，或輕身入敵。 今悉誅吏士，異時亡將必舉軍降虜矣。 」於是但誅牙兵十六輩。
After Fan Chunren left office, Qingchen held sole sway at the Secretariat; he quickly restored the Green Sprouts and Corvée Exemption laws and appointed circuit-wide supervising commissioners. Ambitious for the prime ministership but blocked by Su Zhe, he seized on Zhe's past comparison of the late emperor to Emperor Wu of Han, provoking the throne's wrath; Zhe was dismissed. Zhang Dun had been recalled but had not yet arrived, and Qingchen's ambition for the chancellorship burned brighter. When Zhang Dun finally took office as chancellor, the two men soon fell out again. After Zhang Dun purged a host of officials, he drew up a list of Wen Yanbo, Lü Gongzhu, and thirty others, intending to exile them all to the far south. Qingchen said, "Changing the late emperor's institutions was not without fault, but these men are elders who served many reigns; if we follow Zhang Dun's advice, we will deeply alarm the realm." The emperor asked, "Surely there is a moderate course?" Post the list in the court hall but leave the others alone." When Zhang Xing, garrison commander at Jinming Stockade on the Fuyan frontier, fell in battle, Zhang Dun flew into a rage and proposed putting the entire four-thousand-man garrison to the sword. Qingchen objected, "Generals die in many ways—some storm the walls seeking glory, others throw themselves recklessly at the foe. Execute every man now, and the next time a commander falls, his troops will surrender wholesale to the enemy." In the end only sixteen personal guards were put to death.
8
上幸楚王第，有狂婦人遮道叫呼，告清臣謀反，屬吏捕治，本澶州娼而為清臣姑子田氏外婦者。 清臣不能引去，用御史言，以大學士知河南，尋落職知真定府。
When the emperor visited the Prince of Chu's mansion, a deranged woman blocked the road crying that Qingchen was plotting rebellion. Officials seized her and discovered she was a former Cangzhou prostitute and the mistress of Qingchen's nephew by marriage, surnamed Tian. Unable to resign of his own accord, Qingchen, on the censors' advice, was transferred as grand academician and prefect of Henan; soon he was stripped of his academy title and reassigned to Zhending.
9
初，蔡確子渭上書訴父冤，造奇譖以陷劉摯罪，清臣心知其誣，弗之省，坐奪學士。 徽宗立，入為門下侍郎。 僕射韓忠彥與之有連，惟其言是聽，出范純禮、張舜民，不使呂希純、劉安世入朝，皆其謀也。 尋為曾布所陷，出知大名府而卒，年七十一。 贈金紫光祿大夫。
Earlier, Cai Que's son Wei had petitioned to clear his father's name, inventing outlandish charges to frame Liu Zhe; Qingchen knew the accusations were bogus but failed to look into them, and lost his academy title as punishment. When Huizong took the throne, Qingchen was recalled as vice director of the Chancellery. Grand Counselor Han Zhongyan was allied with him; the emperor listened only to his counsel; Fan Chunli and Zhang Shunmin were ousted, and Lü Xichun and Liu Anshi were kept from court—all at his instigation. Before long Zeng Bu brought him down; he was sent out as prefect of Daming and died there at seventy-one. He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
10
清臣蚤以詞藻受知神宗，建大理寺，築都城，皆命作記，簡重宏放，文體各成一家。 為人寬洪，不忮害。 嘗為舒亶所劾，及在尚書，亶以贓抵罪，獨申救之，曰：「亶信亡狀，然謂之贓則不可。 」再為姚勔所駁，當紹聖議貶，或激使甘心，清臣為之言曰：「勔以職事，所見或不同，豈應以臣故而加重？ 」帝悟，薄勔罪。 起身窮約，以儉自持，至富貴不改。 居官奉法，毋敢撓以私。 然志在利祿，不公於謀國，一意欲取宰相，故操持悖謬，竟不如願以死。 後朝議以復孟后罪，追貶武安軍節度副使，再貶雷州司戶參軍。
Qingchen won Shenzong's favor early for his literary gifts; he was commissioned to write the commemorative records for the new Court of Judicial Review and the capital walls—prose at once terse, weighty, and expansive, each piece a distinct achievement. He was generous by nature and free of malice. Shu Dan had once impeached him; later, when Qingchen headed the Ministry of Personnel, Dan was convicted of corruption, and Qingchen alone interceded: "Dan's conduct was indeed reprehensible, but to call it graft goes too far. Yao Miao had twice blocked his appointments; during the Shaosheng purges some urged heavier punishment for Miao, but Qingchen spoke up: "Miao was performing his duty; officials may disagree—why should he be punished more severely on my account?" The emperor took the point and mitigated Yao Miao's sentence. He rose from poverty and practiced thrift throughout; even in high office he did not change his ways. In office he upheld the law and never bent it for private ends. Yet he was driven by appetite for rank and emolument, not impartial counsel for the realm; obsessed with the prime ministership, his judgment grew reckless, and he died without ever attaining it. A later court, revisiting the wrong done to Empress Meng, posthumously demoted him to deputy military commissioner of Wu'an and then again to revenue clerk at Leizhou.
11
安燾，字厚卿，開封人。 幼警悟。 年十一，從學里中，羞與群兒伍，聞有老先生聚徒，往師之。 先生曰：「汝方為誦數之學，未可從吾遊，當群試省題一詩，中選乃置汝。 」燾無難色。 詩成，出諸生上，由是知名。
An Tao, courtesy name Houqing, was a native of Kaifeng. As a boy he was exceptionally bright. At eleven, while studying locally, he was reluctant to mingle with ordinary boys; learning that an elder scholar nearby was taking disciples, he went to seek instruction. The master told him, "You are still learning rote and arithmetic; you are not ready to study with me. Compose a poem on the provincial examination topic with the other students—if yours is chosen, I will take you in. An Tao did not hesitate. His poem ranked above every other student's, and his name spread from that day.
12
登第，調蔡州觀察推官，至太常丞、主管大名府路機宜文字。 用歐陽修薦，為秘閣校理、判吏部南曹、荊湖北路轉運判官、提點刑獄兼常平、農田水利、差役事。 時方興新法，奉行之吏，或迎合求進。 司農符檄日夜下，如免役增寬剩，造簿供手實，青苗責保任，追胥苛切，其類旁午。 燾平心奉法，列其泰甚於朝。 移使京東路，過闕入見，神宗偉其儀觀，留檢正中書孔目房、修起居注。
After passing the examinations he was posted as judicial aide at Caizhou, eventually rising to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of strategic documents on the Daming Circuit staff. On Ouyang Xiu's recommendation he was appointed Secret Pavilion collator, concurrent reviewer in the Ministry of Personnel's southern bureau, transport judge on the Jinghu North Circuit, and judicial intendant with oversight of Ever-Normal Granary, irrigation, and corvée policy. The New Policies were just being rolled out, and some implementing officials curried favor to win promotion. Orders from the Ministry of Revenue poured in night and day—extra corvée quotas, surplus-tax levies, household-property registers, Green Sprouts guarantors, brutal collection agents—one mandate piled on another. An Tao enforced the law evenhandedly and memorialized the worst abuses to court. Transferred to the Jingdong circuit, he stopped at court for an audience; Shenzong was impressed by his bearing and kept him to audit the Secretariat clerks' office and compile the imperial diary.
13
元豐初，高麗新通使，假燾左諫議大夫往報之。 高麗迎勞，館餼加契丹禮數等，使近臣言：「王遇使者甚敬，出誠心，非若奉契丹苟免邊患而已。 」燾笑答曰：「尊中華，事大國，禮一也，特以罕至有加爾。 朝廷與遼國通好久，豈復於此較厚薄哉！ 」使還，帝以為知禮，即授所假官，兼直學士院。
In the early Yuanfeng era, when Goryeo reopened diplomatic contact, An Tao was temporarily appointed Left Remonstrance Grand Counselor and dispatched in reply. The Goryeo court received him with honors and hospitality matching Khitan protocol; a royal confidant explained, "Our king welcomes your envoy with true respect—it is not the grudging courtesy we show Khitan envoys merely to keep the border quiet. An Tao smiled and replied, "Respect for China and deference to a great power follow the same protocol; you simply add ceremony because our missions are rare. Our court has exchanged envoys with Liao for generations—surely we no longer bother to weigh who shows more favor!" When he returned, the emperor judged him skilled in diplomacy and confirmed his temporary appointment while adding membership in the Hanlin Academy.
14
知審刑院，決剖滯訟五百餘案。 因言：「每蔽獄上省，輕重有疑，則必致駁，勢既不敵，故法官顧避稽停。 請自今以疑獄讞者，皆得輕論。 」從之。 求知陳州，還，為龍圖閣直學士、判軍器監。
As head of the Court for Judicial Review he cleared more than five hundred backlogged cases. He memorialized: "Whenever a decided case goes up to the Secretariat, any dispute over severity draws a reversal; outmatched, judges hold back and cases stall. I ask that hereafter judges may always recommend the lighter penalty when a case is doubtful. The request was granted. He requested assignment as prefect of Chenzhou; on returning to court he was made Hanlin academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and director of the Armaments Directorate.
15
命館遼使。 方宴近郊，使者不令其徒分坐廡下，力爭之，使無以奪。 至肄儀將見，又不使綴行分班，使者入，餘皆坐門外，燾請令門見而出，眾始愧悔。 逮辭日，悉如儀。 或謂細故無足較，燾曰：「契丹喜嘗試人，其漸不可長也。 」俄權三司使，改戶部尚書。 六年。 同知樞密院。
He was assigned to host the Liao envoy. During a banquet in the outer suburbs, the envoy refused to let his retinue sit separately in the side halls; An Tao insisted, and the envoy could not prevail. At the rehearsal for the imperial audience he again tried to keep the retinue from taking their proper places in procession; when the envoy went in alone and the rest were left outside the gate, An Tao insisted they enter and leave by the gate with proper ceremony—only then did they show shame and relent. By the day of departure, all ceremonial requirements were met. Some said these were trifles not worth fighting over; An Tao replied, "The Khitan love to probe for weakness; that habit must not be indulged. Soon he was appointed acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments, then minister of revenue. In the sixth year of Yuanfeng. He became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
16
夏人款塞，乞還侵疆。 燾言：「地有非要害者固宜予，然羌情無厭，當使知吾宥過而息兵，不應示以厭兵之意。 」哲宗立，復仍前議，二府遂欲並棄熙河。 燾固爭之，曰：「自靈武而東，皆中國故地。 先帝有此武功，今無故棄之，豈不取輕於外夷？ 」於是但以葭蘆等四砦歸之。
The Tangut court opened the frontier passes and asked that seized territory be restored. An Tao argued, "Non-critical territory may rightly be returned, but the Tangut appetite is never sated; they must see that we grant clemency and stand down from war—not that we have grown weary of fighting. When Zhezong succeeded to the throne the old proposal resurfaced, and the two chief councils moved to abandon the entire Hexi frontier. An Tao objected strenuously: "From Lingwu eastward lies territory that was once ours. The late emperor won this ground by force of arms; to surrender it without cause—would we not be scorned by the border peoples?" In the end only Jialu and three other forts were returned to the Tanguts.
17
蔡確輩更用事，燾循循其間，不能有所建明。 元祐二年，進知院事。 時復洮、河，擒鬼章青宜結，二邊少清，而幷塞猶苦寇掠。 燾言：「為國者不可好用兵，亦不可畏用兵，好則疲民，畏則遺患。 今朝廷每戒疆吏，非舉國入寇毋得應之，則固畏用兵矣。 雖僅保障戍，實墮其計中，願復講攻擾之策。 且乾順幼豎，梁氏擅權，族黨酋渠多反側顧望。 若有以離間之，未必不回戈而復怨，此一奇也。 」其後夏人自相攜貳，使來修貢，悉如燾策。
When Cai Que and his allies regained influence, An Tao kept a circumspect distance and could put forward nothing of consequence. In the second year of Yuanyou (1087), he was promoted to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Hexi had been retaken and the Qiang chief Qingyijie captured, bringing a measure of quiet to both frontiers—yet the garrison towns along the Shanxi border still endured constant raids. An Tao argued, "A state must neither be eager for war nor afraid of it—eagerness exhausts the people, fear leaves trouble to fester. The court now repeatedly warns frontier officials not to respond unless the enemy mounts a full-scale invasion—that is already to fear war. We may think we are only holding the line, but in truth we play into their design; I ask that we revive the strategy of offensive raids and harassment. Moreover Emperor Qianshun is still a youth, the Liang clan holds power in its grip, and many tribal chiefs and clan leaders are divided and wavering. If we can drive wedges among them, they may well turn on one another in renewed enmity—that would be a singular opportunity. Soon afterward the Tanguts fell to infighting among themselves and sent envoys to resume tribute—precisely as An Tao had foreseen.
18
宣仁太后患國用不足，頗裁冗費，宗室奉亦在議中。 燾諫曰：「陛下雖痛抑外家，以示至公，然此舉不可不深思而熟計。 」太后悟，遂止。
Empress Dowager Xuanren, troubled by insufficient state revenues, moved to cut wasteful spending; even the stipends paid to members of the imperial clan came under review. An Tao remonstrated, "Your Majesty may wish to restrain the empress's kin severely so as to show perfect impartiality, but this step deserves the deepest thought and the most careful reckoning. The empress dowager took his point and dropped the proposal.
19
大河北流，宰相主水官議，必欲回之東注。 燾以河流入濼淀，久必淤淺，恐河朔無以禦敵，遂上言曰：「自小吳未決之前，河雖屢徙，而盡在中國，故京師得以為北限。 今決而西，則河尾益北，如此不已，將南岸遂屬敵界。 彼若建橋梁，守以州郡，窺兵河外，可為寒心。 今水官之議，不過論地形，較功費； 而獻納之臣，不考利害輕重，徒便於治河，而以設險為緩，非至計也。 」帝雖然之，而回河之議紛起，東北蕭然煩費，功亦不就。
The Yellow River was flowing northward; the chief councillor backed the hydraulic engineers and pressed to divert it back east. An Tao argued that if the river were sent into the Luo marshes it would inevitably silt up and shoal, leaving Hebei without a natural barrier against invasion. He memorialized: "Before the Xiaowu breach, the river shifted many times, yet always remained within our territory, so the capital could rely on it as the northern limit. Now that it has broken westward, the river's lower reach keeps drifting north; if this goes on, the south bank will eventually lie within enemy territory. Should they build bridges, hold the crossings with prefectural garrisons, and probe for weakness beyond the river—the prospect is enough to make one shudder. The hydraulic engineers debate only topography and the cost of labor; and the courtiers who urge adoption never weigh the larger stakes. They fixate on ease of river management and treat strategic defense as an afterthought—that is no sound policy. The emperor agreed in principle, but debate over diverting the river raged on; the northeast was drained by the effort, and in the end the work was never completed.
20
三年，同列皆序遷，且新用執政，燾獨如初。 詔增其兩秩，燾懇辭曰：「是雖有故事，竊意以一時同列超升之故，特用是以慰安其心爾。 今日願自臣革之，使朝廷不為姑息，而大臣稍敦廉恥之風，庶或有補。 」竟不受。 以母憂去，卒喪，拜觀文殿學士、知鄭州，徙潁昌及河南府，入為門下侍郎。
In the third year of Yuanyou his colleagues were all promoted in turn and new men took the highest offices, yet An Tao alone received no advancement. An edict came to raise him two ranks in rank. An Tao earnestly declined: "There is precedent for such a grant, but I suspect it was devised only to console colleagues who had been passed over when others were promoted ahead of them. Let me be the one to break that custom, so the court ceases to indulge favoritism and senior officials recover some sense of honor and shame—it may do a little good. He refused the promotion to the end. He left office to mourn his mother. When the mourning period ended he was made Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred to Yingchang and Henan Prefecture, and finally recalled as vice director of the Chancellery.
21
宣仁之喪，宗室既為三年服，才越歲，章惇拜相，欲革為期。 燾爭之曰：「上以先后保佑之久，追崇如恐不盡，茲用明道故實耳。 遽改之，播諸天下，非佳聲也。 」乃止。 燾與惇布衣交，覬其助己，燾不肯少下之。 陽翟民蓋漸有財訟，而與諫官來之邵交通，開封得其事。 惇右之邵，欲薄其罪，燾不可； 復欲並劾開封，燾又不可，遂與惇隙。 明堂齋祠，為儀仗使，後官有絕馳道穿仗而過者，燾方舉劾，諫官常安民又言，教坊不當於相國寺作樂。 帝怒，欲逐安民，燾為救釋。 惇遂譖其相表裏，出知鄭州，徙大名。
At Empress Dowager Xuanren's funeral the imperial clan had already begun three-year mourning; scarcely a year later Zhang Dun became chief councillor and sought to shorten it to one year. An Tao objected: "The throne granted such honors because the late empress had guarded the dynasty for so long—fearing that no tribute could be enough. The Mingdao precedents were chosen for that reason. To alter that now and proclaim the change to the empire would not reflect well on the court. The change was abandoned. An Tao and Zhang Dun had been friends since their days as commoners. Zhang Dun expected An Tao's support; An Tao would not yield to him in the least. A Yangdi resident named Gai Jian was embroiled in a property dispute and had improper contact with the remonstrance official Lai Zhishao; Kaifeng Prefecture uncovered the affair. Zhang Dun took Lai Zhishao's side and tried to minimize his guilt; An Tao would not agree; Zhang Dun then tried to impeach Kaifeng Prefecture as well; An Tao again refused—and the two men broke with each other. During the Hall of Brightness fasting rites, where he served as ceremonial guard commissioner, palace women cut straight across the imperial processional way through the guard lines. An Tao was preparing to impeach them when the remonstrance official Chang Anmin also protested that the Music Bureau should not perform at Xiangguo Temple. The emperor was furious and wanted to banish Chang Anmin; An Tao intervened and secured his pardon. Zhang Dun then accused them of colluding inside and outside the court. An Tao was sent out to serve as prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred to Daming.
22
父日華，本三班院吏，以燾恩封光祿大夫，至是卒，年九十餘，燾免喪。 徽宗立，復知樞密院。 舊制，內侍出使，以所得旨言於院，審實乃得行。 後多輒去，燾請按治之。 都知閻守懃領他職，祈罷不以告，亦劾之，帝敕守懃詣燾謝。 郝隨得罪，或揣上意且起用，欲援赦為階，亦爭之。
His father An Rihua had begun as a clerk in the Three-Rank Courtyard and, through his son's favor, had been ennobled as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. He now died at more than ninety; An Tao completed the mourning rites. When Emperor Huizong took the throne, An Tao was again appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Under the old rules, when palace eunuchs were dispatched on missions they had to report the orders they had received to the bureau and could not act until the instructions were verified. In time many simply departed without doing so; An Tao asked that they be investigated and punished. The chief eunuch Yan Shougong had taken another appointment and petitioned for release without informing the bureau; An Tao impeached him as well, and the emperor ordered Yan Shougong to go to An Tao and apologize. Hao Sui had fallen from favor; some, reading the emperor's mind, expected his imminent recall and sought to use the general amnesty as a pretext for reinstatement. An Tao opposed that too.
23
以老避位，帝將寵以觀文殿大學士，有間之者曰：「是宰相恩典也。 」但以學士知河南。 將行，上疏曰：「自紹聖、元符以來，用事之臣，持紹述之名，誑惑君父，上則固寵位而快恩仇，下則希進用而肆朋附。 彼自為謀則善矣，未嚐有毫髮為公家計者也。 夫聽言之道，必以其事觀之。 臣不敢高談遠引，獨以神考之事切於今者為證。 熙寧、元豐之間，中外府庫，無不充衍，小邑所積錢米，亦不減二十萬，紹聖以還，傾竭以供邊費，使軍無見糧，吏無月俸，公私虛耗，未有甚於此時，而反謂紹述，豈不為厚誣哉！ 願陛下監之，勿使飾偏辭而為身謀者復得行其說。 」又言：「東京黨禍已萌，願戒履霜之漸。 」語尤激切。
As he stepped aside on account of age, the emperor meant to honor him with the title Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature. A detractor whispered, "That is a boon reserved for chief councillors. He received only the lower rank of academician and was made prefect of Henan. Before leaving the capital he submitted a memorial: "Since the Shaosheng and Yuanfu reigns, the men who have held power under the banner of 'continuing the legacy' have misled their sovereign—above, to cling to favor and settle old scores; below, to win promotion and indulge faction. They schemed ably for themselves, but never spared so much as a thought for the public weal. The proper way to weigh words is to judge them by their results. I will not indulge in lofty rhetoric or distant precedents; I cite only what touches the present from the reign of the late Emperor Shenzong. Under the Xining and Yuanfeng reigns, treasuries at every level overflowed; even small counties held no less than two hundred thousand in cash and grain. Since Shaosheng the state has been bled dry to pay for the frontier, until soldiers have no rations in hand and officials no monthly pay. Never has waste been so severe—yet they call this 'continuing the legacy.' What gross deception is this! I beg Your Majesty to take warning, and not allow those who cloak self-interest in one-sided arguments to prevail again. He added, "Faction strife at the Eastern Capital has already begun; Your Majesty should heed the warning that great troubles start from small signs." His language was especially forceful and urgent.

初，建青唐邈川為湟州，戍守困於供億。 燾在樞府，因議者以為可棄，奏還之。 崇寧元年議其罪，降端明殿學士，再貶寧國軍節度副使，漢陽軍安置。 湟州復，又降祁州團練副使。 鄯州之復，又移建昌軍，然棄鄯州時，燾居憂不預也，終不敢自明。 閱再歲，始復通議大夫，還洛卒，年七十五。 後五歲，悉還其官職。
When Qingtang Miaochuan was first made into Huangzhou Prefecture, the garrison struggled under the burden of supply. An Tao, then serving at the Privy Council, joined those who argued the post should be abandoned and memorialized for its withdrawal. In Chongning 1 (1102), his case was reviewed. He was stripped to Scholar of the Hall of Enlightened Governance, then demoted again to Vice Commissioner of the Ningguo Army and exiled under restraint to Hanyang. When Huangzhou was retaken, he was demoted once more to Vice Regimental Trainer at Qizhou. When Shanzhou was retaken, he was reassigned to Jianchang Army. But he had been in mourning when Shanzhou was given up and had played no part in that decision; to the end he did not dare defend himself. Two years later he was restored to Grand Master for Glorious Manifestation. He returned to Luoyang, where he died at seventy-five. Five years after that, all his former ranks were posthumously restored.

子扶，靖康時為給事中。 金人入京師，責取金帛，扶與梅執禮、陳知質、程振皆見殺。
His son Fu was Supervising Censor at the time of the Jingkang crisis. After the Jin entered the capital and demanded gold and silk tribute, Fu was executed together with Mei Zhili, Chen Zhizhi, and Cheng Zhen.

張璪，初名琥，字邃明，滁州全椒人，洎之孫也。 早孤，鞠於兄環，欲任以官，辭不就。 未冠登第，歷鳳翔法曹、縉雲令。
Zhang Can, originally named Hu, courtesy name Suiming, was a native of Quanjiao in Chuzhou and a grandson of Zhang Ji. Left fatherless young, he was raised by his elder brother Huan, who sought to place him in office, but he refused. He passed the examinations before coming of age and served successively as judicial clerk at Fengxiang and magistrate of Jinyun.
27
王安石與環善，既得政，將用之，而環已老，乃引璪同編修中書條例，授集賢校理、知諫院、直舍人院。 楊繪、劉摯論助役，安石使璪為文詰之，辭，曾布請為之，由是忤安石意。 神宗欲命璪知制誥，安石薦用布，以璪同修起居注。 自縣令至是，才歲餘。 坐奏事不實，解三職，已而復之。
Wang Anshi, who was close to Huan, planned to appoint him once he took power, but Huan was already elderly. Wang therefore brought Can in to help revise the Central Secretariat regulations and gave him collator's rank in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, the post of remonstrance officer, and duty in the Drafting Academy. When Yang Hui and Liu Zhi criticized the corvée-exemption law, Anshi asked Can to draft a rebuttal; Can refused. Zeng Bu volunteered instead, and Can thereby fell from Anshi's favor. Shenzong meant to appoint Can Drafting Academician, but Anshi put Bu in that role and relegated Can to compiling the imperial diary. It had been barely more than a year since he left the county magistracy. He lost all three offices for an inaccurate memorial but was soon reinstated.
28
時建議武學，璪言：「古之太學，舞干習射，受成獻功，莫不在焉。 文武之才，皆自此出，未聞偏習其一者也。 請無問文武之士，一養於太學。 」朝廷既復河、隴，欲因勢戡定夔、蜀、荊、廣諸夷，璪言：「先王務治中國而已。 今生財未盡有道，用財未盡有禮，不宜遽及徂征之事。 」皆不聽。 以集賢殿修撰知蔡州，復知諫院兼侍御史知雜事。
When plans were drawn up for a military academy, Can argued, "The ancient Grand Academy combined shield drill and archery with civil instruction and the ceremonies for presenting students' accomplishments—nothing was left out. Civil and military talent alike came from that single school; there was no tradition of cultivating one to the exclusion of the other. Let civil and military students alike be educated together in the Grand Academy. After the court retook the He and Long regions, it planned to push on into the tribal territories of Kuizhou, Sichuan, Jing, and Guang. Can said, "The sage kings of old concerned themselves with governing China alone. We have not yet fully realized the Way in producing wealth or in spending it with ritual restraint; this is no time to launch distant campaigns. The court ignored all of it. As Academician-Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he was appointed prefect of Caizhou and again given charge of the remonstrance bureau and the supervising censorate.
29
盧秉行鹽法於東南，操持峻急，一人抵禁，數家為黥徙，且破產以償告捕，二年中犯者萬人。 璪條列其狀。 又言：「行役法以來，最下戶亦每歲納錢，乞度寬羨數均損之，以惠貧弱。 」後皆施行。
Lu Bing's enforcement of the salt monopoly in the southeast was merciless: a single offense could send whole households into tattooed exile, while ruined families paid informants' bounties; within two years ten thousand people were convicted. Can laid out these abuses in detail. He also urged that, because the corvée-exemption levy now fell even on the poorest households each year, surplus collections be recalculated and the burden equalized to relieve the indigent. Both recommendations were eventually adopted.
30
鄭俠事起，璪媚呂惠卿，劾馮京與俠交通有跡，深其辭，致京等於罪。 判司農寺，出知河陽。 元豐初，入權度支副使，遂知制誥、知諫院。 判國子監，薦蔡卞可為直講。 建增博士弟子員，月書、季考，歲校，以行藝次升，略仿《周官》鄉比之法，立齋舍八十二。 學官之盛，近代莫比，其議多自璪發之。
During the Zheng Xia affair Can aligned himself with Lü Huiqing, accused Feng Jing of proven contact with Xia, embroidered the charges, and secured convictions against Feng and others. He was appointed chief of the Ministry of Revenue's agricultural directorate, then sent out as prefect of Heyang. Early in Yuanfeng he entered court as acting Vice Commissioner of Revenue and soon became Drafting Academician and remonstrance officer. As director of education he recommended Cai Bian for a lectureship. He expanded the quota of doctoral students, instituted monthly progress reports, quarterly exams, and annual reviews with promotion by character and achievement in rough imitation of the Zhou rite of local comparison, and built eighty-two dormitory halls. The state academies had never enjoyed such prosperity in living memory, and most of the reforms were Can's doing.
31
蘇軾下臺獄，璪與李定雜治，謀傅致軾於死，卒不克。 詳定郊廟奉祀禮文，議者多以國朝未嘗躬行方澤之禮為非，正詔議更制。 璪請於夏至之日，備禮容樂舞，以塚宰攝事。 帝曰：「在今所宜，無以易此。 」卒行其說。 為翰林學士，詳定官制，以寄祿二十四階易前日省、寺虛名，而職事名始正。
When Su Shi was thrown into the Censorate prison, Can joined Li Ding in investigating him and tried to frame him on a capital charge, but failed. In revising suburban and ancestral ritual texts, many argued that the dynasty had never performed the Fangze sacrifice in person; the emperor ordered the rites redrafted. Can proposed restoring the Fangze rite on the summer solstice with full ceremonial, music, and dance, the chief minister standing in for the emperor. The emperor replied, "This is exactly what the times require; there is no better alternative. Can's plan was adopted in the end. As Hanlin Academician he helped reform the bureaucracy, substituting twenty-four salary grades for the hollow provincial and directorate titles of earlier days and aligning office names with actual work.
32
四年，拜參知政事，改中書侍郎。 哲宗立，諫官、御史合攻之，謂：「璪奸邪便佞，善窺主意，隨勢所在而依附之，往往以危機陷人。 深交舒亶，數起大獄，天下共知其為大奸。 小人而在高位，德之賊也。 」疏入，皆不報。 最後，劉摯言：「璪初奉安石，旋附惠卿，隨王珪，黨章惇，諂蔡確，數人之性不同，而能探情變節，左右從順，各得其歡心。 今過惡既章，不可不速去。 」如是逾歲，乃以資政殿學士知鄭州，徙河南、定州、大名府，進大學士，知揚州以卒。 贈右銀青光祿大夫，諡曰「簡翼」。
In the fourth year he received appointment as Vice Grand Councillor with the title Vice Director of the Secretariat. After Zhezong's accession, remonstrance officers and censors assailed him together, declaring, "Can is a sycophant who reads the throne's mood, attaches himself to every faction in turn, and routinely traps rivals with dangerous charges. He was close to Shu Dan and repeatedly stirred up major prosecutions; throughout the realm he was known as an arch-villain. A villain in high place is the enemy of public morals. The memorials went in; none drew a reply. At last Liu Zhi wrote, "Can first served Anshi, then quickly clung to Huiqing, followed Wang Gui, joined Zhang Dun's faction, and flattered Cai Que—very different men, yet he could read each one, shift his allegiance, and accommodate himself until he won every patron's favor. His misconduct is now manifest; he should be dismissed without delay. A year passed before he was finally removed, appointed Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred through Henan, Dingzhou, and Daming, promoted to Grand Academician, and died in office at Yangzhou. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Silver Lustre Grand Master of the Palace, with the posthumous name Jianyi ("Simple and Steadfast").

蒲宗孟
Pu Zongmeng
34
蒲宗孟，字傳正，閬州新井人。 第進士，調夔州觀察推官。 治平中，水災地震，宗孟上書，斥大臣及宮禁、宦寺，熙寧元年，改著作佐郎。 神宗見其名，曰：「是嘗言水災地震者邪？ 」召試學士院，以為館閣校勘、檢正中書戶房兼修條例，進集賢校理。
Pu Zongmeng, style name Chuanzheng, was a native of Xinjing in Langzhou. After placing among the jinshi, he was assigned as investigating assistant magistrate in Kuizhou. In the Zhiping period, after floods and earthquakes, Zongmeng memorialized the throne, attacking senior ministers along with the inner palace and the eunuch bureaucracy. In the first year of Xining he was made Assistant Editorial Director. When Emperor Shenzong saw his name, he asked, "Isn't this the man who once warned about floods and earthquakes? " He was called to the Hanlin Academy for examination and appointed collator in the Palace Library, rectifier in the Central Secretariat's Revenue Section with concurrent work on regulatory revisions, and then promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
35
時三司新置提舉帳司官，祿豐地要，人人欲得之。 執政上其員，帝命與宗孟。 命察訪荊湖兩路，奏罷辰、沅役錢及湖南丁賦，遠人賴之。 呂惠卿制手實法，然猶許災傷五分以上不預。 宗孟言：「民以手實上其家之物產而官為注籍，以正百年無用不明之版圖而均齊其力役，天下良法也。 然災傷五分不預焉。 臣以為使民自供，初無所擾，何待豐歲？ 願詔有司，勿以豐凶弛張其法。 」從之，民於是益病矣。
The Three Commissions had just created ledger-supervisor posts—lucrative and powerful—and every official wanted one. When the chief ministers submitted their nominees, the emperor gave the appointment to Zongmeng. Commissioned to inspect the Jing and Hu circuits, he memorialized to abolish corvée payments in Chen and Yuan and the household levy in Hunan, to the great relief of people in the frontier districts. Lü Huiqing drafted the hand-real-property law, but still exempted households that had suffered disaster losses of fifty percent or more. Zongmeng argued, "When households declare their property under the hand-real system and the state registers it, century-old land records are finally brought into order and corvée burdens equalized. For the empire this is an excellent law. Yet households with disaster losses of fifty percent are still left out. I believe self-reporting imposes no real hardship in the first place—why should the law wait for a good harvest year? I ask that Your Majesty instruct the responsible agencies not to relax or tighten the law according to whether the harvest is good or bad. " The emperor agreed, and the people were burdened all the more.
36
俄同修起居注、直舍人院、知制誥，帝又稱其有史才，命同修兩朝國史，為翰林學士兼侍讀。 舊制，學士唯服金帶，宗孟入謝，帝曰：「學士職清地近，非他官比，而官儀未寵。 」乃加佩魚，遂著為令。 樞密都承旨張誠一預書局事，頗肆橫，挾中旨以脅同列。 宗孟持其語質帝前，皆非是，因叩頭白其奸。 帝察其不阿，欲大用，拜尚書左丞。
Soon he was also compiling the imperial diary, serving in the Drafting Academy, and appointed Drafting Academician. The emperor again praised his historical talent and ordered him to co-author the national history of two reigns, making him Hanlin Academician and Reader-in-Waiting. Under the old rule, academicians wore only the gold belt. When Zongmeng came to give thanks, the emperor said, "An academician's post is exalted and close to the throne, unlike ordinary offices, yet the ceremonial honors accorded the rank have been insufficient. " He therefore granted him the fish tally as well, and the practice was written into regulation. Zhang Chengyi, chief coordinator at the Bureau of Military Affairs, took part in the history project and behaved with great arrogance, wielding secret imperial instructions to bully his colleagues. Zongmeng repeated Zhang's claims before the emperor and showed that none held up, then kowtowed to denounce his wrongdoing. Seeing that he would not truckle to power, the emperor meant to promote him further and appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
37
帝嘗語輔臣，有無人才之歎，宗孟率爾對曰：「人才半為司馬光邪說所壞。 」帝不語，直視久之，曰：「蒲宗孟乃不取司馬光邪？ 未論別事，只辭樞密一節，朕自即位以來，唯見此一人； 他人，則雖迫之使去，亦不肯矣。 」宗孟慚懼，至無以為容。 僅一歲，御史論其荒於酒色及繕治府舍過制，罷知汝州。 逾年，加資政殿學士，徙、杭、鄆三州。
Once, lamenting the shortage of capable men, the emperor spoke to his chief ministers, and Zongmeng blurted out, "Half our talent has been spoiled by Sima Guang's perverse doctrines. " The emperor fell silent, fixed his gaze on him for a long moment, and said, "So Pu Zongmeng considers Sima Guang heterodox, does he? Never mind other questions—in refusing the Bureau of Military Affairs alone, since I took the throne I have seen only one man do such a thing; the rest, even if you drove them out, would not go. " Zongmeng was mortified and afraid, scarcely able to hold himself together. Barely a year later, censors charged him with dissipation in wine and women and with building his official residence beyond what regulations allowed; he was removed and made prefect of Ruzhou. The following year he was made Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and served in succession at Xu, Hang, and Yun prefectures.

鄆介梁山濼，素多盜，宗孟痛治之，雖小偷微罪，亦斷其足筋，盜雖為衰止，而所殺亦不可勝計矣。 方徙河中，御史以慘酷劾，奪職知虢州。 明年，復知河中，還其職。 帥永興，移大名。 宗孟厭苦易地，頗默默不樂，復求河中。 卒，年六十六。
Yunzhou bordered Liangshan Marsh and had long been infested with bandits. Zongmeng cracked down ruthlessly: even for petty theft he severed the Achilles tendons. Banditry did subside, but the dead were beyond counting. As he was being transferred to Hedong, censors impeached him for cruelty; he was demoted and sent to serve as prefect of Guozhou. The next year he returned to Hedong and regained his former rank. He served as military commissioner at Yongxing, then moved to Daming. Weary of constant transfers, Zongmeng grew withdrawn and discontented and asked to return to Hedong. He died at sixty-six.

宗孟趣尚嚴整而性侈汰，藏帑豐，每旦刲羊十、豕十，然燭三百入郡舍。 或請損之，慍曰：「君欲使我坐暗室忍饑邪？ 」常日盥潔，有小洗面、大洗面、小濯足、大濯足、小大澡浴之別。 每用婢子數人，一浴至湯五斛。 他奉養率稱是。 嘗以書抵蘇軾云：「晚年學道有所得。 」軾答之曰：「聞所得甚高，然有二事相勸：一曰慈，二曰儉也。 」蓋針其失云。
Zongmeng favored strict formality but lived extravagantly. His stores were ample: each morning he had ten sheep and ten pigs slaughtered, and three hundred candles lit when he entered the prefectural compound. When someone suggested he economize, he snapped, "Do you expect me to sit in the dark and go hungry? " His daily grooming had separate categories: small face-washing, large face-washing, small foot-washing, large foot-washing, and small and large bathing. Several maids attended each session, and a single bath could use as much as five hu of water. The rest of his household spending matched this scale. He once wrote Su Shi, "In my later years I have cultivated the Way and feel I have gained something. " Su Shi answered, "I hear your attainment is lofty indeed, yet I would counsel you in two matters: first, compassion; second, frugality. " It was a pointed rebuke of his failings.

黃履，字安中，邵武人。 少遊太學，舉進士，調南京法曹，又為高密、廣平王二宮教授、館閣校勘，同知禮院。 擢監察御史裏行，辭御史，改崇政殿說書兼知諫院。
Huang Lü, style name Anzhong, was a native of Shaowu. As a youth he studied at the Imperial Academy and passed the jinshi examination. He served as judicial clerk at the Southern Capital, tutor to the Princes of Gaomi and Guangping, collator in the Palace Library, and deputy director of the Ministry of Rites. Promoted to acting investigating censor, he declined the censorate and was made lecturer at the Hall of Exalted Governance while also heading the Remonstrance Bureau.

神宗嘗詢天地合祭是非，對曰：「國朝之制，冬至祭天圓丘，夏至祭地方澤，每歲行之，皆合於古。 猶以有司攝事未足以盡，於是三歲一郊而親行之，所謂因時制宜者也，雖施之方今，為不可易。 惟合祭之非，在所當正。 然今日禮文之失，非獨此也，願敕有司正群祀，為一代損益之制。 」詔置局詳定，命履董之，北郊之議遂定。 同修起居注，進知制誥、同修國史。 遭母憂去，服除，以禮部尚書召。
When Shenzong asked whether the combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth was correct, Huang Lü answered, "The dynasty sacrifices Heaven at the Round Mound at the winter solstice and Earth at the Square Pond at the summer solstice, each year as the ancients did. Because having ministers perform the rites by proxy still seemed inadequate, every three years the emperor conducts the suburban sacrifice in person—an adaptation to the times that should not be altered even now. Only the combined sacrifice itself is what must be set right. Today's ritual errors go beyond this one point. I ask that Your Majesty order the responsible offices to revise the entire sacrificial code and establish a balanced ritual system for the age. " The throne ordered a review bureau under Lü's direction, and the northern suburban sacrifice was settled. He also compiled the imperial diary, was promoted to Drafting Academician, and helped compile the National History. He left office upon his mother's death and, after the mourning period, was recalled as Minister of Rites.

時閩中患苦鹽法，獻言者眾，神宗謂履自閩來，恃以為決。 履乃陳法甚便，遂不復革，鄉論鄙之。 遷御史中丞。 履以大臣多因細故罰金，遂言：「賈誼有云：『遇之以禮，則群臣自喜。 』群臣且然，況大臣乎？ 使罪在可議，黜之可也； 可恕，釋之可也，豈可罰以示辱哉！ 」時又制侍郎以下不許獨對，履言：「陛下博訪萬務，雖遠外微官，猶令獨對，顧於侍從乃弗得願也。 」遂刊其制。 御史翟思言事，有旨詰所自來。 履諫曰：「御史以言為職，非有所聞，則無以言。 今乃究其自來，則人將懲之，臺諫不復有聞矣，恐失開言路之意。 」事乃寢。
Fujian was then groaning under the salt monopoly, and memorials poured in. Shenzong, knowing Lü was a Fujian man, looked to him for the decisive answer. Lü declared the law perfectly workable, and reform was dropped. His neighbors at home despised him for it. He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief. Noting that many senior ministers were being fined for trifling offenses, Lü said, "Jia Yi wrote, 'Receive them with courtesy, and the ministers will rejoice of themselves. ' If that holds for ordinary ministers, how much more for great ministers? If guilt is doubtful, remove them; if it can be forgiven, pardon them. How can fines be used merely to humiliate! " A rule then barred vice-ministers and lower ranks from private audience. Lü protested, "Your Majesty seeks counsel on every matter under heaven; even humble officials from afar may speak with you privately—yet your close attendants may not. " The rule was amended. When Investigating Censor Zhai Si memorialized on a matter, the throne ordered him to reveal his source. Lü remonstrated, "A censor lives by speaking out. Without something he has heard, he has nothing to report. If you trace every report to its source, men will hold back; the censorate and remonstrance bureau will fall silent, and the avenue of frank speech will be lost. The inquiry was dropped.

先是，北郊之論雖定，猶不果行，履又建言：「陽復陰消，各因其時。 上圓下方，各順其體。 是以聖人因天祀天，因地祀地，三代至漢，其儀不易。 及王莽諂事元后，遂躋地位，同席共牢，歷世襲行，不能全革。 逮神宗考古揆今，以正大典，嘗有意於茲矣。 今承先志，當在陛下及二三執政。 」哲宗詢諸朝，章惇以為北郊止可謂之社。 履曰：「天子祭天地。 蓋郊者交於神明之義，所以天地皆稱郊。 故《詩序》云『郊祀天地』。 若夫社者，土之神而已，豈有祭大祇亦謂之社乎？ 」哲宗可之，遂定郊議。 拜尚書右丞。
Although the northern suburban rite had been decided, it had not yet been implemented. Lü memorialized again: "When yang returns and yin withdraws, each has its season. Heaven is round and Earth is square; each sacrifice should follow its nature. The sages sacrificed to Heaven as Heaven and to Earth as Earth; from the Three Dynasties through Han the rites remained unchanged. Wang Mang, flattering Empress Dowager Yuan, elevated Earth's rank and placed Heaven and Earth on one mat with a shared offering—a practice that persisted for generations without full reform. When Shenzong studied antiquity to set the great rites right for his own age, he had already turned his mind to this question. To carry forward that intent now falls to Your Majesty and your leading ministers. " Zhezong asked the court, and Zhang Dun argued that the northern suburban rite could only be termed a she sacrifice. Lü replied, "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. Jiao means communion with the divine; that is why sacrifices to both Heaven and Earth are called jiao. Hence the preface to the Book of Songs speaks of 'the jiao sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.' She, by contrast, is the god of the soil alone. How could a sacrifice to great Earth itself be called she? " Zhezong agreed, and the suburban rite was finally settled. He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

會正言鄒浩以言事貶新州，履曰：「浩以親被拔擢之故，敢犯顏納忠，陛下遽斥之死地，人臣將視以為戒，誰復敢為陛下論得失乎？ 乞徙善地。 」坐罷知亳州。 徽宗立，召為資政殿學士兼侍讀，復拜右丞。 未逾年，求去，加大學士、提舉中太一宮，卒。

Officials will take warning—who will dare discuss your policies again? I ask that he be transferred to a milder post. " For this he was removed and made prefect of Bozhou. When Emperor Huizong took the throne, Lü was recalled as Scholar of the Hall of Proclaimed Governance and Reader-in-Waiting and again made Right Vice Director. Within the year he asked to retire, was made Grand Academician and supervisor of the Palace of Central Grand Unity, and died.

論曰：哲宗親政之初，見慮未定，范、呂諸賢在廷，左右弼謨，俾日邇忠讜，疏絕回遹，以端其志向，元祐之治業，庶可守也。 清臣怙才躁進，陰覬柄用，首發紹述之說，以隙國是，群奸洞之，衝決莫障，重為薦紳之禍焉。 至於興大獄以傾馮京、蘇軾者，璪也； 助成手實之法，以壞人材、讕司馬光者，宗孟也； 訐垂簾之事，擊呂大防、劉摯等去之者，履也。 清臣真小人之靡，三子抑其亞乎。 燾論議識趣，有可稱述，雖立朝無附，而依違蔡確、章惇間，無所匡建，非大臣之道也。
The commentators write: When Zhezong first took personal rule, his mind was still unsettled. With Fan, Lü, and other worthy ministers at court to guide him, he might daily have drawn closer to honest counsel and kept sycophants at bay, fixing his course so that the gains of the Yuanyou era could have been preserved. Li Qingchen, arrogant in his talent and hungry for advancement, secretly coveted real power. He first preached the "restore the ancestral way" doctrine, splitting the court over national policy. Once the villains saw the breach, nothing could hold them back, and the scholar-official class suffered anew. Raising great prosecutions to ruin Feng Jing and Su Shi—that was Zhang Can; helping perfect the hand-real-property law to ruin talent and defame Sima Guang—that was Pu Zongmeng; denouncing the regency and driving out Lü Dafang, Liu Zhi, and the rest—that was Huang Lü. Qingchen was the basest sort of petty man; the other three were scarcely better. Tao's views and judgment deserve mention, yet though he stood apart in court he vacillated between Cai Que and Zhang Dun and built nothing of lasting worth—not the conduct of a great minister.

蔡挺，字子政，宋城人。 第進士，調虔州推官。 秩滿，以父希言當官蜀，乞代行，遂授陵州團練推官。 王堯臣安撫陝西，辟管勾文字。 富弼使遼，奏挺從，至雄州，誓書有所更易，遣挺還白。 仁宗欲知契丹事，召對便殿，挺時有父喪，聽以衫帽入。
Cai Ting, style name Zizheng, was a native of Songcheng. After passing the jinshi examination he was made assistant magistrate of Qian Prefecture. When his term ended, his father Xi Yan was slated for appointment in Shu; Ting asked to go in his place and was made regiment assistant magistrate of Ling Prefecture. Wang Yao Chen, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, took him on as document officer. When Fu Bi went on embassy to Liao, he asked that Ting accompany him. At Xiong Prefecture the treaty text had been changed, and Fu sent Ting back to report. Emperor Renzong, wanting intelligence on the Khitan, summoned Ting to the side hall. Ting was in mourning for his father but was allowed to appear in everyday dress.

Fan Zhongyan, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and Hedong, recommended Ting as military vice-prefect of Jing Prefecture; he was later transferred to Yan Prefecture. Banditry was rife in Hebei, and prefects were chosen with care; Ting was appointed prefect of Bo Prefecture. He ordered the subordinate counties to tighten the mutual-responsibility system, seized several harborers of bandits, canceled their old debts, and enrolled them as clerks to watch and report. Thereafter bandits were caught as soon as they struck. He equalized tax assessments in Boing and Liaocheng counties, yielding tens of thousands of cash each year. The Three Departments Commission promulgated his method empire-wide, but in effect it raised taxes.

為開封府推官、提點府界公事。 部修六漯河，用李仲昌議，塞北流，入於六漯。 一夕復決，兵夫芟楗漂溺不可計。 降知滁州，言者以為輕，乃貶秩停官。

He oversaw repairs on the Six Lou Rivers, following Li Zhongchang's plan to dam the northern channel and redirect it into the Six Lou system. Overnight the dike burst again; soldiers and laborers were swept away and drowned in numbers beyond count. He was demoted to prefect of Chuzhou, but critics deemed the punishment too lenient, so his rank was cut further and his appointment suspended.

越數歲，稍起知南安軍，提點江西刑獄，提舉虔州鹽。 自大庾嶺下南至廣，驛路荒遠，室廬稀疏，往來無所芘。 挺兄抗時為廣東轉運使，乃相與謀，課民植松夾道，以休行者。 江閩鹽賊率千百為州縣害，挺諭所部與期，使首納器甲，原其罪，得兵械萬計。 官鹽惡而價貴，盜鹽善而價且下，故私販日滋。 挺簡僚吏至淮轉新鹽，明殿賞，以官數之餘畀之，於是賊黨破散，宿弊遂絕，歲增賣鹽四十萬。
Several years later he was gradually restored to office as military prefect of Nan'an, judicial commissioner for Jiangxi, and salt commissioner for Qianzhou. From the foot of Dayu Ridge south to Guang, the post road was bleak and remote, houses few and far between, and travelers had no shelter along the way. Ting's elder brother Kang was then transport commissioner of Guangdong; the two of them devised a plan to require the people to plant pines along both sides of the road so travelers could rest in the shade. Salt smugglers in Jiang and Fujian banded together by the hundreds and thousands to plague the prefectures and counties. Ting ordered his jurisdiction to set a deadline: those who surrendered weapons first would be pardoned, and more than ten thousand arms were turned in. Official salt was poor in quality yet expensive, while smuggled salt was better and its price kept falling, so private trafficking grew day by day. Ting dispatched officials to the Huai region to bring in fresh salt, openly promised rewards, and let them keep whatever exceeded the official quota. The smuggling gangs then broke apart, long-standing abuses ended, and annual salt sales rose by four hundred thousand units.

改陝西轉運副使，進直龍圖閣、知慶州，因上書論攻守大計。 夏人大入，挺盡斂邊戶入保，戒諸砦無出戰。 諒祚親帥軍數萬攻大順，挺料城堅不可破，而柔遠城惡，亟遣總管張玉將銳師守之。 先布鐵蒺藜大順城旁水中，騎渡水多躓，驚言有神。 過三日不克，諒祚督帳下決戰，挺伏強弩壕外，飛矢貫其鎧，遂引卻。 移寇柔遠，玉夜斫營，夏人驚擾潰去。 環州熟羌思順舉族投諒祚，倚為鄉導。 挺宣言思順且復來，命葺其舊舍，出兵西為迎候之舉。 諒祚果疑思順，毒之死。 挺築城馬練平為荔原堡，分屬羌三千人守之。
He was made vice transport commissioner of Shaanxi, promoted to direct associate of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Qingzhou, and submitted a memorial setting out the grand strategy of attack and defense. When the Tanguts invaded in force, Ting gathered every border household into fortified stockades and ordered the forts not to engage outside the walls. Liangzuo personally led tens of thousands of troops against Dashun. Ting reckoned that city's walls too strong to take, but Rouyuan was poorly fortified, so he urgently sent commander Zhang Yu with crack troops to hold it. He first scattered iron caltrops in the water beside Dashun; cavalry crossing the stream kept stumbling, and in alarm they cried that spirits were at work. After three days without success, Liangzuo drove his personal guard to a decisive assault. Ting had strong crossbows hidden beyond the moat; a bolt pierced his armor, and he pulled back. The enemy turned on Rouyuan; Zhang Yu raided their camp by night, and the Tangut army broke in panic and fled. Sishun, a naturalized Qiang chieftain of Huanzhou, brought his whole clan over to Liangzuo and served as his local guide. Ting announced that Sishun was about to return, had his old house restored, and sent troops west as though to welcome him back. Liangzuo did grow suspicious of Sishun and had him poisoned to death. Ting fortified Malianping as Liyuan Stockade and posted three thousand Qiang tribesmen to hold it.

神宗即位，加天章閣待制、知渭州。 舉籍禁兵悉還府，不使有隱占。 建勤武堂，五日一訓之，偏伍鉦鼓之法甚備。 儲勁卒於行間，遇用奇，則別為一隊。 甲兵整習，常若寇至。 又分義勇為伍番，番三千人，參正兵防秋與春，以八月、正月集，四十五日而罷，歲省粟帛、錢緡十三萬有奇。 括並邊生地冒耕田千八百頃，募人佃種，以益邊儲。 取邊民闌市蕃部田八千頃，以給弓箭手。 又築城定戎軍為熙寧砦，開地二千頃，募卒三千人耕守之。
When Emperor Shenzong acceded, Ting was made editorial acolyte of the Tianzhang Pavilion and prefect of Weizhou. He conducted a full muster of the palace troops and returned every man to the prefectural rolls, tolerating no hidden retention. He built the Hall of Diligent Military Training and drilled the men every five days; the squad formations with gongs and drums were fully systematized. He held crack troops in reserve within the ranks; when a surprise maneuver was needed, they formed a separate detachment. Arms and armor were kept in fighting trim, and training went on as though the enemy were always at the gates. He also divided the volunteer militia into five rotations of three thousand men each to support regular troops in the autumn and spring defenses; they assembled in the eighth and first months, served forty-five days, and were dismissed, saving more than one hundred thirty thousand in grain, cloth, and cash each year. He surveyed and consolidated eighteen hundred qing of illegally cultivated border land, recruited tenants to farm it, and thereby increased frontier stores. He reclaimed eight thousand qing of tribal land that border settlers had seized in illicit market dealings and assigned it to archer-soldiers. He also fortified Dingwu Army as Xining Stockade, opened two thousand qing of land, and recruited three thousand soldiers to farm and garrison it.

諜告夏人集胡盧河，挺出奇兵迎擊之。 夏人潰，分諸將躡而討之，蕩其七族。 進右諫議大夫，賜金帛三千。 夏人復犯諸砦，環慶兵不能禦，挺遣張玉以萬人往解其圍。 慶州軍變，挺討平之，進龍圖閣直學士。 廣銳卒徙營，眾憚遷，欲為亂，城中震擾，挺推斬首惡十九人，訖徙營。 蕃部歲饑，以田質於弓箭手，過期輒沒。 挺為貸官錢，歲息什一，後遂推為蕃漢青苗、助役法。 又自以意製渡河大索及兵械鐮槍，皆獲其用。
Spies reported the Tanguts massing at Hulu River; Ting sent a surprise force to intercept them. The Tangut force broke; he sent his generals in pursuit and destroyed seven clans. He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grand Master and rewarded with three thousand in gold and silks. The Tanguts again struck the stockades; the Huan and Qing garrisons could not hold them, so Ting sent Zhang Yu with ten thousand men to break the siege. A mutiny erupted in the Qingzhou garrison; Ting put it down and was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion. When the Guangrui troops were ordered to move camp, the men feared the transfer and plotted mutiny, throwing the city into uproar. Ting tried and executed nineteen ringleaders and saw the relocation through. In famine years tribal peoples pawned their fields to archer-soldiers; once the term expired, the land was forfeited. Ting lent them official funds at ten percent annual interest; the practice was later extended as the Green Sprouts and corvée-assistance programs for tribes and Han settlers alike. He also devised on his own great ropes for river crossings and weapons such as sickle-spears, all of which proved effective in the field.

In the winter of the seventh year, while reporting to the throne he was struck by illness and collapsed. The emperor came in person to give him medicine and relieved him of office, appointing him Academic Bachelor of the Hall of Zizheng and judge of the Nanjing Remaining Imperial Censorate. In the second year of the Yuanfeng era he died, at the age of sixty-six. He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Minsu, "Keen and Solemn."
55
挺譎而多知，人莫能窺其城府。 初，為富弼、范仲淹客，頗泄其幾事於呂夷簡以自售。 在渭久，鬱鬱不自聊，寓意詞曲，有「玉關人老」之歎。 中使至，則使優伶歌之，以達於禁掖。 神宗湣焉，遂有樞密之拜云。 兄抗抗，字子直。 中進士，調太平州推官。 聞父疾，委官去。 稍遷睦親宅講書。 英宗在宮邸，器重之，請於安懿王，願得與遊。 每見，必衣冠盡禮，義兼師友。 再遷太常博士、通判秦州，為秘閣校理，乞知蘇州。 州並江湖，民田苦風潮害，抗築長堤，自城屬昆山，亙八十里，民得立塍堨，大以為利。
Ting was cunning and resourceful; no one could read his inner mind. Early on, while serving as a retainer to Fu Bi and Fan Zhongyan, he leaked many of their confidential plans to Lü Yijian to advance his own career. After long service at Weizhou he grew restless and despondent, and poured his feelings into song lyrics, lamenting that he was "growing old at Jade Gate Pass." When palace envoys visited, he had actors perform the songs so they would reach the inner court. Emperor Shenzong took pity on him, and this is how he came to receive appointment to the Bureau of Military Affairs. Elder brother: Kang. Kang, courtesy name Zizhi. He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial officer of Taiping Prefecture. When he learned his father was ill, he resigned his post and went home. He was gradually promoted to lecturer at the Hall of Imperial Kinship. While still in the princely residence, Emperor Yingzong held Kang in high regard, asked Prince Anyi for permission, and wished to keep his company. Whenever they met, the prince always dressed in full ceremonial garb and treated Kang with complete propriety, honoring him as both teacher and friend. He was further promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice prefect of Qinzhou, then made collator of the Secret Archive, and requested appointment as prefect of Suzhou. The prefecture bordered lakes and rivers, and the people's fields suffered from wind and tidal flooding. Kang built a long dike from the city wall to Kunshan, eighty li in length, so farmers could raise embankments and levees—a great benefit to the region.
56
徙廣東轉運使。 岑水銅冶廢，官給虛券為市，久不償。 人無所取資，聚而私鑄，抗盡給之，人得直以止。 番禺歲運鹽英、韶，道遠，多侵竊雜惡。 抗命十舸為一運，擇攝官主之，歲終會其殿最，增十五萬緡。
He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangdong. The Censhui copper smeltery had shut down; the government paid with worthless vouchers that for years went unredeemed. With no other source of income, people turned to illicit smelting. Kang paid them all in full, and once they received fair value the illegal casting stopped. Each year Panyu shipped salt to Yingde and Shaoguan; the route was long, and much was stolen or adulterated along the way. Kang ordered ten boats to a convoy, chose acting officials to oversee each shipment, and assessed their performance at year's end; revenue rose by one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.
57
英宗立，召為三司判官。 廣部去京師遠，不即至，帝見南來者必問之。 及入對，諭曰：「卿乃吾故人，朕望於卿者厚，勿以常禮自疏也。 」以史館修撰同知諫院。 方議安懿王典禮，抗引禮為人後之誼，指陳切至，涕淚被面，帝亦感泣。 都城大水，抗請見，帝迎問之，抗推原變異，守前說以對。 大臣畏其諫列，白為知制誥，遷龍圖閣直學士、知定州。 帝惜其去，曰：「第行，且召矣。」
When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Kang was summoned to serve as judicial official of the Three Departments Commission. Guangdong was far from the capital and Kang did not arrive promptly; whenever the emperor saw anyone coming from the south he would ask after him. When he appeared for audience, the emperor told him, "You are an old friend of mine; I expect much of you—do not hold yourself apart with ordinary formalities." He was made compiler of the Historiography Institute and associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau. While the court was debating the rites for Prince Anyi, Kang invoked the proprieties of adoption and succession, arguing with force and precision until tears streamed down his face; the emperor wept too. When the capital was flooded, Kang requested an audience; the emperor came forward to question him. Kang traced the cause of the disaster and held to his earlier argument in reply. The chief ministers feared his remonstrances and had him made drafter of edicts, then transferred him as direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Dingzhou. The emperor regretted losing him and said, "Go for now—you will be recalled soon."
58
郡兵番戍，室家留營多不謹，夫歸輒首原，抗下令悉按以法，戍者感焉。 帝不豫，趣命為太子詹事，未至而神宗立，改樞密直學士、知秦州。 過闕，帝見之，悲慟不自勝，曰：「先帝疾大漸，猶不忘卿。 」遂赴鎮。
When prefectural troops rotated to frontier duty, the families they left behind in camp were often lax; when the men returned they always pardoned them. Kang ordered every offense prosecuted by law, and the garrison troops were deeply moved. When the emperor fell ill, Kang was urgently appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; before he could take up the post, Emperor Shenzong acceded and he was reassigned as direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qinzhou. Passing through the capital, he was received by the emperor, who was overcome with grief and said, "When the late emperor's illness was grave, he still did not forget you." He then proceeded to his post.
59
秦有質院，質諸羌百餘人，自少至老，扃繫之，非死不出，抗皆縱釋，約毋得擅相仇殺。 已而有犯者，斬以徇，莫敢奸令。 居數日，夢英宗召語，眷如平生，欲退復留。 覺為家人言，感念歔欷。 及靈駕發引之旦，東望號慟，見僚佐於便室，驟得疾卒，年六十。 特贈禮部侍郎。 又欲賜諡，吳奎曰：「抗以舊恩，自雜學士贈官，已逾常制。 」遂止。
Qinzhou maintained a hostage compound holding more than a hundred Qiang tribesmen from youth to old age, locked away and released only in death. Kang freed them all and bound them by oath not to take private revenge on one another. When someone later broke the oath, he was beheaded as a public warning, and none dared defy the order. After several days he dreamed that Emperor Yingzong summoned him to talk; their affection was as in life; he wished to leave but was kept back. When he awoke he told his family and wept with emotion. On the morning the imperial coffin set out, he looked eastward and wailed in grief; meeting his staff in a side room, he was suddenly stricken and died, at the age of sixty. He was specially posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites. The court also wished to grant a posthumous title. Wu Kui said, "Out of old favor, Kang has already been posthumously promoted from miscellaneous academician—a step beyond ordinary precedent." The proposal was dropped.
60
王韶，字子純，江州德安人。 第進士，調新安主簿、建昌軍司理參軍。 試制科不中，客遊陝西，訪采邊事。
Wang Shao, courtesy name Zichun, was a native of De'an in Jiangzhou. He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Xin'an and judicial administrator of Jianchang Army. He failed the special decree examination, traveled in Shaanxi as a guest scholar, and gathered intelligence on frontier affairs.
61
熙寧元年，詣闕上《平戎策》三篇，其略以為：
In the first year of the Xining era he came to court and submitted three chapters of the "Strategy for Pacifying the Barbarians," the gist of which was as follows:
62
「西夏可取。 欲取西夏，當先復河、湟，則夏人有腹背受敵之憂。 夏人比年攻青唐，不能克，萬一克之，必並兵南向，大掠秦、渭之間，牧馬於蘭、會，斷古渭境，盡服南山生羌，西築武勝，遣兵時掠洮、河，則隴、蜀諸郡當盡驚擾，瞎征兄弟其能自保邪？ 今唃氏子孫，唯董氈粗能自立，瞎征、欺巴溫之徒，又法所及，各不過一二百里，其勢豈能與西人抗哉！ 武威之南，至於洮、河、蘭、鄯，皆故漢郡縣，所謂湟中、浩、大小榆、枹罕，土地肥美，宜五種者在焉。 幸今諸羌瓜分，莫相統一，此正可並合而兼撫之時也。 諸種既服，唃氏敢不歸？
"The Western Xia can be taken. To take the Western Xia, we must first recover the He and Huang regions; then the Tanguts will face enemies on both front and rear. In recent years the Tanguts have attacked Qingtang without success; if they should take it, they will surely combine their forces and drive south, plundering heavily between Qin and Wei, pasturing horses at Lanzhou and Huizhou, cutting off the Gulu frontier, subduing all the raw Qiang south of the mountains, building Wusheng to the west, and sending raiders against Tao and He—then the prefectures of Longxi and Shu will all be thrown into alarm. Can Xiazheng and his brothers protect themselves? Today among the Gus clan, only Dong Zhan can roughly hold his own; Xiazheng, Qibawen, and their kind fall within Tangut reach, each controlling no more than one or two hundred li—how can their strength resist the Western Xia! South of Wuwei, as far as Tao, He, Lan, and Shan, all were former Han commanderies and counties—the so-called Huangzhong, Hao, Greater and Lesser Yu, and Baohan—where the land is fertile and rich and suited to the five grains. Fortunately the Qiang tribes are now divided and none holds unified authority—this is precisely the moment to combine and win them over together. Once the various tribes submit, would the Gus dare not come over?
63
唃氏歸則河西李氏在吾股掌中矣。 且唃氏子孫，瞎征差盛，為諸羌所畏，若招諭之，使居武勝或渭源城，使糾合宗黨，制其部族，習用漢法，異時族類雖盛，不過一延州李士彬、環州慕恩耳。 為漢有肘腋之助，且使夏人無所連結，策之上也。」
If the Gus come over, the Li clan of Hexi will be in the palm of our hand. Moreover, among the Gus' descendants Xiazheng is relatively strong and feared by the other Qiang. If we summon and win him over, settle him at Wusheng or Weiyuan, have him rally his clansmen, control his tribes, and accustom them to Han law, then even if his people grow strong in time they will be no more than a Li Shibin of Yanzhou or a Mu En of Huanzhou. The Song would gain allies at their very side, and the Tanguts would have no one to link up with—this is the best strategy of all."
64
神宗異其言，召問方略，以韶管幹秦鳳經略司機宜文字。
The emperor was struck by his words, summoned him to discuss strategy, and appointed Shao staff officer for planning in the Qinfeng Circuit Military Commission.
65
蕃部俞龍珂在青唐最大，渭源羌與夏人皆欲羈屬之，諸將議先致討。 韶因按邊，引數騎直抵其帳，諭其成敗，遂留宿。 明旦，兩種皆遣其豪隨以東。 久之，龍珂率屬十二萬口內附，所謂包順者也。
Among the tribes, Yu Longke at Qingtang was the most powerful; the Weiyuan Qiang and the Tanguts both sought to bring him under their sway, and the generals debated attacking him first. While inspecting the frontier, Shao led a few horsemen straight to Longke's tent, explained the prospects of victory and defeat, and stayed the night. At dawn the next day, both tribes sent their chieftains to follow him east. Before long, Longke led one hundred twenty thousand followers to submit to the court—the so-called Baoshun tribe.
66
韶又言：「渭源至秦州，良田不耕者萬頃，願置市易司，頗籠商賈之利，取其贏以治田。 」帝從其言，改著作佐郎，仍命韶提舉。 經略使李師中言：「韶乃欲指占極邊弓箭手地耳，又將移市易司於古渭，恐秦州自此益多事，所得不補所亡。 」王安石主韶議，為罷師中，以竇舜卿代，且遣李若愚按實。 若愚至，問田所在，韶不能對。 舜卿檢索，僅得地一頃，既地主有訟，又歸之矣。 若愚奏其欺，安石又為罷舜卿而命韓縝。 縝遂附會實其事，師中、舜卿皆坐謫，而韶為太子中允、秘閣校理。 後帥郭逵上韶盜貸市易錢，安石以為不足校，徙逵涇原。
Shao further said, "From Weiyuan to Qinzhou there are ten thousand qing of good land lying uncultivated. I wish to establish a market-control office to capture merchants' profits and use the surplus to develop the fields." The emperor accepted his proposal, promoted him to Assistant Editorial Director, and ordered Shao to supervise the project. Circuit commissioner Li Shizhong said, "Shao merely wishes to seize archer-soldiers' lands on the extreme frontier and will move the market-control office to ancient Weizhou. I fear Qinzhou will only grow more troubled—the gains will not make up for the losses." Wang Anshi supported Shao's proposal, had Shizhong removed and replaced with Dou Shunqing, and sent Li Ruoyu to investigate. When Ruoyu arrived and asked where the land was, Shao could not answer. Shunqing searched and found only one qing of land; since the landowner had a lawsuit pending, it was returned. Ruoyu memorialized that Shao had deceived them; Anshi again had Shunqing removed and appointed Han Zhen. Han Zhen then colluded to confirm the matter; Shizhong and Shunqing were both demoted and exiled, while Shao was made Palace Attendant and collator of the Secret Archive. Later commander Guo Kui memorialized that Shao had embezzled market-control funds; Anshi held it not worth investigating and transferred Kui to Jingyuan.

帝志復河、隴，築古渭為通遠軍，以韶知軍事。 五年七月，引兵城渭源堡及乞神平，破蒙羅角、抹耳水巴等族。 初，羌保險，諸將謀置陣平地，韶曰：「賊不舍險來鬥，則我師必徒歸。 今已入險地，當使險為吾有。 」乃徑趣抹邦山，壓敵軍而陣，令曰：「敢言退者斬！ 」賊乘高下鬥，師小卻。 韶躬擐甲胃，麾帳下兵逆擊之，羌大潰，焚其廬帳而還，洮西大震。 會瞎征度洮為之援，餘黨復集。 韶命別將由竹牛嶺路張軍聲，而潛師越武勝，遇瞎征首領瞎藥等，與戰破之，遂城武勝，建為鎮洮軍。 進右正言、集賢殿修撰。 復擊走瞎征，降其部落二萬。 更名鎮洮為熙州，以熙、河、洮、岷、通遠為一路，韶以龍圖閣待制知熙州。
The emperor was resolved to recover the He and Long regions; ancient Weizhou was fortified as Tongyuan Army, and Shao was made its military administrator. In the seventh month of the fifth year, he led troops to fortify Weiyuan Stockade and Qishenping and defeated the Mengluojiao, Mo'ershuiba, and other tribes. At first the Qiang held the defiles; the generals planned to deploy on level ground. Shao said, "If the enemy will not leave the defiles to fight, our army must return empty-handed." We have already entered dangerous ground; we must make the defiles ours. Thereupon he pressed straight for Mobang Mountain, deployed pressing against the enemy, and ordered, "Whoever speaks of retreat shall be beheaded!" The enemy fought from higher ground; the army fell back slightly. Shao donned armor himself, commanded his personal guard to counterattack, the Qiang broke in great rout, their lodges and tents were burned, and the west of the Tao was greatly shaken. Just then Xiazheng crossed the Tao to bring reinforcements, and the remaining bands gathered again. Shao ordered a separate general to take the Zhuniu Ridge route to feign troop movements while secretly leading his army over Wusheng; they encountered Xiazheng's chieftains Xiayao and others, defeated them, fortified Wusheng, and established it as Zhentao Army. He was promoted to Right Rectifier and compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. He again attacked and drove off Xiazheng, and twenty thousand of his tribes submitted. Zhentao was renamed Xizhou; Xi, He, Tao, Min, and Tongyuan were made one circuit, and Shao was made editorial acolyte of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Xizhou.
68
六年三月，取河州，遷樞密直學士。 降羌叛，韶回軍擊之。 瞎征以其間據河州，韶進破訶諾木藏城，穿露骨山，南入洮州境，道狹隘，釋馬徒行，或日至六七。 瞎征留其黨守河州，自將尾官軍，韶力戰破走之，河州復平。 連拔宕、岷二州，疊、洮羌酋皆以城附。 軍行五十有四日，涉千八百里，得州五，斬首數千級，獲牛、羊、馬以萬計。 進左諫議大夫、端明殿學士。 七年，入朝，又加資政殿學士，賜第崇仁坊。
In the third month of the sixth year he took Hezhou and was transferred to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. The submitted Qiang rebelled; Shao turned his army and struck them. Xiazheng took advantage of the interval to seize Hezhou. Shao advanced, broke Henuomucang city, passed through Lougu Mountain, and entered Taozhou territory; the road was narrow and steep, so they abandoned their horses and went on foot, sometimes covering only six or seven li a day. Xiazheng left his followers to hold Hezhou and personally tailed the imperial army; Shao fought hard, broke them, and drove them off, and Hezhou was pacified again. He took Dang and Min prefectures in succession; the chieftains of Die and Tao all submitted their cities. The army marched fifty-four days, covered eighteen hundred li, gained five prefectures, beheaded several thousand, and captured cattle, sheep, and horses by the tens of thousands. He was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grand Master and academician of the Hall of Duanming. In the seventh year he entered court, was further made Academic Bachelor of the Hall of Zizheng, and granted a residence in Chongren Ward.
